introduction: In competitive exams, keyboard shortcuts require strict rote memorization. This foundational tier covers the universal file management and text formatting shortcuts that apply identically across Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

core_concepts.title: Basic File Operations
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + N`: Create a New document/workbook.
- `Ctrl + O`: Open an existing document.
- `Ctrl + S`: Save the current document.
- `Ctrl + P`: Print the document.
- `Ctrl + W`: Close the current document.

core_concepts.title: Universal Text Formatting
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + B`: Apply or remove Bold formatting.
- `Ctrl + I`: Apply or remove Italic formatting.
- `Ctrl + U`: Apply or remove Underline formatting.

core_concepts.title: The Big Four (Editing)
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + C`: Copy the selected text or item.
- `Ctrl + X`: Cut the selected text or item.
- `Ctrl + V`: Paste the copied/cut item.
- `Ctrl + Z`: Undo the last action.

important_entities.name: Ctrl + A
important_entities.significance: Instantly selects all text, images, and content within the active document or active Excel worksheet.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants often logically guess that 'Paste' starts with P, so the shortcut must be `Ctrl + P`. This is a classic trap. `Ctrl + P` is strictly for Print. Paste is `Ctrl + V`.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Look at the bottom row of your keyboard. The core editing shortcuts are literally placed right next to each other in a line for easy access: Z (Undo), X (Cut), C (Copy), V (Paste).

exam_strategy_tips: For Tier-1 exams, if a question asks how to quickly 'save' ongoing work to prevent data loss, the answer is always `Ctrl + S`.
